description: Wire-protocol fixture suite. Each case describes one HTTP round-trip the SDK MUST conform to. The 58-tuple parity-corpus tests *evaluation* semantics; this suite tests the *wire layer* (304/ETag/error classes/malformed body) which is otherwise implicitly per-SDK. Consumers live at apps/sdk-*/tests/wire/wire-cases.{ext} and ingest this file at runtime — DO NOT duplicate cases per language. Error classes are normalised: each SDK maps its own SdkErrorCode-style enum onto {fetchFailed, timeout, parseFailed, invalidSdkKey}. Request side (1.3, #803): a case may pin the SDK key (given.sdkKey, a valid key from sdk-key-shapes.json — except request-path-malformed-key, whose inline malformed key pins FR-001's one-segment url.PathEscape) and the exact parsed request path (expected.requestPath, query excluded); a consumer MUST configure the SDK with given.sdkKey when present and MUST FAIL on any expected field it does not read, so a new expectation can never be skipped silently. Schema validated at load-time via wire-cases.schema.json (Draft 2020-12). See epic #146 + #148 + spec 112 for the contract-testing framework.

errorClasses.fetchFailed: Non-2xx HTTP (except 304/403/404), or network error, or unreadable body.
errorClasses.timeout: Request aborted by SDK timeout (not dispose).
errorClasses.parseFailed: Body was 200 but JSON.parse threw OR shape did not match {p, f, s}.
errorClasses.invalidSdkKey: CDN responded 403 or 404 — the SDK key was rejected upstream.

cases.description: Initial fetch — server returns 200 + body + ETag. SDK ingests the body and remembers the ETag.
Conditional GET — SDK supplies the previous ETag; server returns 304 with no body. SDK retains its cached config and does not re-parse.
Cache rotation — SDK supplies the previous ETag; server returns 200 with a new ETag and refreshed body. SDK swaps cached body and updates stored ETag.
Transient backend failure — server returns 503. SDK reports a typed fetch-failed error; cached config (if any) is preserved by the caller.
Invalid SDK key path — CDN returns 404. SDK reports the typed invalid-sdk-key error class (distinct from generic fetch-failed so callers can surface a different message).
Server returns 200 with garbage body. SDK reports a typed parse-failed error; cached config (if any) is preserved by the caller.

Server returns 200 with valid JSON of the wrong top-level shape ({foo: 'bar'} instead of {p, f, s}). SDK reports parse-failed — same error class as malformed-json since both are 'body cannot become a config'.

Server returns 401 Unauthorized with no body. 401 is NOT a ConfigCat invalid-SDK-key status (only 403/404 are) — it is a generic, retryable fetch failure. The SDK reports fetchFailed (matching configcat-js, which classes everything outside {200, 304, 403, 404} as a transient fetch error).

The edge's real answer to an unknown SDK key (#918): 403 with ConfigCat's AccessDenied XML, byte for byte what tools/test-harness-live-contract/reference-origin/src/index.ts serves on a KV miss (and what packages/contract/read-path-transcript.json records from the CDN Worker). The live harness serves it for an unseeded key, so every live suite meets the origin's own miss, not a fault. ConfigCat parity: 403 — like 404 — means 'your SDK Key seems to be wrong' (a non-retryable invalid-key signal, NOT a transient fetch failure), whatever the body says. configcat-js classes 403 and 404 together; the SDK reports invalidSdkKey for both.

Server returns 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header. The SDK reports a generic fetchFailed — smart-retry / Retry-After honouring is deliberately out of scope (epic #146 sub-task E). This case only pins that 429 is a transient fetch failure (not an invalid-key signal) and that the SDK does not choke on the Retry-After header.

Server returns 304 Not Modified carrying a Last-Modified header but NO ETag. With no prior ETag and no ETag on the 304, the SDK must NOT manufacture a cache validator from Last-Modified — it surfaces notModified with a null resulting ETag. Confirms ETag is the SOLE cache validator (no Last-Modified fallback), matching configcat-js.

SDK configured with a non-default base URL; server responds 200 with a body + ETag. Verifies the SDK honours its configured baseUrl (options.baseUrl / DataGovernance custom equivalent) — the outgoing request URL must begin with the custom base, and the fetch still succeeds. Consumers read given.baseUrl and assert expected.requestUrlPrefix.

Server never responds within the SDK's configured request timeout. The SDK aborts the in-flight request and reports the timeout error class — distinct from a generic network failure (fetchFailed). No config is ingested. behavior=timeout: the nominal status/headers are never delivered.

Connection closed mid-response: the server begins delivering a 200 body, then the socket drops before the body completes. The SDK surfaces fetchFailed (a network/transport failure) — NOT parseFailed, because a truncated body is not a JSON-shape error. No config is ingested. behavior=close-mid-response: the partial body is config-v6.boolean.json, cut off mid-stream.

The exact request path for a legacy key (#803, FR-001). The SDK is configured with given.sdkKey — taken from sdk-key-shapes.json, never a per-SDK literal — and MUST request <baseUrl>/configuration-files/<sdkKey>/config_v6.json with the key's exact bytes: no /v2/ prefix, no hash or cache-key tail of the key. A legacy key has no '/', so it is one segment as-is. Consumers compare the PARSED PATH of the recorded request to expected.requestPath exactly; the query string is excluded (the version carrier, #807, may add one).

The exact request path for a ConfigCat-shaped key, configcat-sdk-1/<22>/<22> (#803, FR-001). A well-shaped key travels RAW, as every ConfigCat SDK sends it: its three '/'-separated parts stay three path segments — exactly a stock ConfigCat SDK's bytes, not '%2F'-escaped into one segment, not hashed, no /v2/ prefix. given.sdkKey comes from sdk-key-shapes.json. Consumers compare the PARSED PATH of the recorded request to expected.requestPath exactly; the query string is excluded (#807 may add one).

The exact request path for a MALFORMED key (#803, FR-001). A key that fails the shape check of sdk-key-shapes.json is escaped into ONE path segment with Go's url.PathEscape: it keeps only A-Z a-z 0-9, the four unreserved marks - _ . ~ and the six sub-delims $ & + : = @; every other byte (/ ; , ? # % space ! ' ( ) * included, and all non-ASCII UTF-8 bytes) becomes %XX with uppercase hex. That is NOT encodeURIComponent (which keeps ! ' ( ) * and escapes $ & + : = @), nor a URL library's lenient path quoting. The key carries a space, every reserved character, '/', '?', '#', '%', one non-ASCII character of each UTF-8 length (U+00E9 'é' = 2 bytes C3 A9, U+20AC '€' = 3 bytes E2 82 AC, U+1F600 '😀' = 4 bytes F0 9F 98 80, outside the BMP so a UTF-16 surrogate pair in JS/Java/C#/Dart/Kotlin/Swift strings) and a trailing '..', so any other escaper — one that escapes UTF-16 code units, Latin-1 bytes or lowercase hex, or drops/replaces a non-ASCII character — or one that lets the key leave its segment, produces a different path. Unlike the other request-path cases, given.sdkKey is NOT from sdk-key-shapes.json: it is malformed by design, and scripts/validate-wire-cases.ts names this case as the only exception and checks requestPath against FR-001. expected.requestPath is real `go run` output of url.PathEscape. The SDK still fetches (only the empty key, '.' and '..' are refused) and the server answers a plain 200. Consumers compare the PARSED PATH of the recorded request, still percent-encoded as sent, to expected.requestPath exactly; the query string is excluded (#807 may add one).
